title: BUG: launch sync mass-deleted ~230 downloaded albums as 'stale'
description: Repro (Tim 2026-06-11): synced a ~230-album collection, most downloaded; relaunched after a rebuild; syncCollection removed all downloaded albums as 'stale'. ROOT CAUSE: DownloadManager.syncCollection's removal pass is fail-destructive. (1) currentAlbumIDs comes from collectionAlbums, which reads the LOCAL album_collections junction that the app-launch refresh rewrites moments earlier — an empty/partial read returns [] WITHOUT error, making every offline album 'stale'. (2) The keep-it guard consults the SAME junction (collectionIDs(forAlbum:)), so when the junction is the broken thing, the guard fails open and removeDownload nukes everything. (3) Separate resume flaw: the download pass skips any album with >=1 offline track (allOfflineAlbumIDs membership), so interrupted album downloads never complete via sync. FIXES: empty-membership guard (an empty synced collection is a failed fetch, never a remove-everything signal); scope stale candidates to albums whose junction lists THIS collection (junction emptiness becomes fail-SAFE, and individually-downloaded albums are never auto-removed); resume partials via offlineStatus instead of the any-track set.
close_reason: Three fixes in DownloadManager.syncCollection: (1) empty membership list = failed/raced fetch -> reconciliation skipped entirely (the launch refresh rewrites the junction this read depends on, so empty-without-error was the mass-delete trigger); (2) stale candidates scoped to albums whose junction lists THIS collection — junction emptiness now fails SAFE, and manually-downloaded / other-collection albums are never auto-removed; (3) partially-downloaded albums resume via offlineStatus check instead of being skipped for having >=1 track. 3 tests reproduce the disaster (empty membership deleted everything; not-owned albums deleted; partial never resumed) and pin the fixes. Re-download of the nuked collection: re-marking it synced now resumes exactly the missing albums/tracks.

title: Lock-screen Pause doesn't stick: track keeps ending and auto-advancing while paused
description:
REPRO (on device): Shuffle a collection. Lock the screen. Tap Pause on the lock screen. A couple minutes later the NEXT song starts playing on its own. Tap Pause again -> a couple minutes later another song starts. Pause is not actually stopping/holding playback; the engine continues to end-of-track and auto-advances while supposedly paused.

SEVERITY: P0 — pause is fundamentally broken from the lock screen (background).

HYPOTHESES to investigate:
- Remote MPRemoteCommandCenter pause handler may not reach engine.pause()/queue.pause(), so audio keeps playing to end -> handleTrackEnded -> next track (the ~couple-minutes interval ~= remaining track length, and it repeats per track).
- OR a background-safe DispatchSourceTimer (crossfade trigger) keeps firing while paused and advances. Verify CrossfadeEngine.pause() cancels all timers and the active AVAudioPlayer actually pauses in background.
- Possibly surfaced/changed by the d12 audio-session change (#76) — verify pause behavior under the new non-ducking .playback session.

Files: NowPlayingBridge.swift (remote command handlers), CrossfadeEngine.pause() / handleTrackEnded() / scheduleCrossfadeTriggerIfNeeded(), QueueManager.pause().
design:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by staff review, all cited): CrossfadeEngine.wireInterruptions() at CrossfadeEngine.swift:500-510. onInterruptionEnded discards shouldResume (the '_ in' at :504) and resumes whenever 'playbackState == .paused' (:507-508) — it cannot tell a USER pause from an INTERRUPTION pause. So when any interruption-ended fires while the user has manually paused, it auto-resumes; the track then plays to EOF, handleTrackEnded() runs (now .playing, passes guard :419) and advances the queue. Repeats per track. Matches repro exactly.

PROVEN BY ELIMINATION (only path that can move a paused track in background):
- EOF callback cannot fire while paused: PlayerSlot.pause() -> AVAudioPlayer.pause(); audioPlayerDidFinishPlaying only fires at real EOF (PlayerSlot.swift:48-50, 75-79).
- Crossfade trigger + ramp DispatchSourceTimers ARE cancelled on pause: CrossfadeEngine.swift:127,129. So no background timer fires beginCrossfade after manual pause.
- No other resume/play path runs while locked+backgrounded: queue.resume() only from AppRouter.resumePlayback() / NowPlayingBridge playCommand (foreground taps). Observation loop only writes MPNowPlayingInfo.
- QueueManager idle auto-advance needs .idle (QueueManager.swift:456); manual pause sets .paused (CrossfadeEngine.swift:131-132). No advance.
=> onInterruptionEnded->resume() is the ONLY viable mechanism. Since the symptom occurs, interruption-ended events ARE firing (no device log needed to prove the mechanism; the source of the interruption is irrelevant to the fix). #76 (.duckOthers removed) plausibly increases the rate of real interruption-ended events under a non-mixable session, surfacing the latent bug.

shouldResume IS available and is being discarded: AudioSession.handleInterruption decodes it and passes to onInterruptionEnded (AudioSession.swift:97-100), proven by AudioSessionTests:48-88. The OTHER engine (AVQueuePlayerEngine) already honors it (PlaybackEngineTests:205-211) — CrossfadeEngine is the inconsistent one.

FIX (refined per review): add 'private var pausedByInterruption = false'.
- Set true ONLY in onInterruptionBegan (around/before the pause() call).
- onInterruptionEnded(shouldResume): 'guard pausedByInterruption, shouldResume else { pausedByInterruption = false; return }'; then configureForPlayback + resume + clear flag. HONOR shouldResume (stop using '_ in').
- Clear flag=false in play() and resume(). Do NOT touch the flag inside pause()/stop() — pause() is shared by the interruption handler AND the user path (MPRemoteCommandCenter.pauseCommand -> queue.pause -> engine.pause), so inferring origin from pause() or from playbackState is wrong. Clearing on every interruption-ended (both branches) + on play/resume covers the user-pause-after-failed-resume case (review Hole C).

TESTS (failing-first, CrossfadeEngineTests + audio-session mock):
1. Manual pause is NOT auto-resumed: play -> user pause() -> fire interruptionEnded(shouldResume:true) -> still .paused, no resume on active slot.
2. Interruption pause IS resumed: play -> interruptionBegan -> interruptionEnded(shouldResume:true) -> .playing.
3. shouldResume:false stays paused even for an interruption pause.
4. User pause DURING an interruption is not auto-resumed on ended.

VERIFY ON DEVICE: repro gone (pause holds while locked); a genuine phone-call interruption still auto-resumes after.
close_reason: Fixed + verified on device (PR #79): lock-screen pause now holds; interruption-ended only auto-resumes an interruption-initiated, system-resumable pause. 4 new tests green.

title: Graceful fallback when offline file:// missing -> re-resolve to stream
description: Today dangling file:// fails playback with no recovery.
design:
DEPENDS ON Lunara-uww.3.1 (which folds in 3.2). Do this AFTER the 3.1/3.2 resolver PR lands — it builds directly on PlaybackURLResolving.

WHAT 3.1 ALREADY SOLVES (do not re-implement)
OfflineStore.localFileURL(forTrackID:) (Lunara/Library/Offline/OfflineStore.swift:13-31) already calls FileManager.fileExists; if the offline file is missing on disk it deletes the stale OfflineTrackRecord row and returns nil. The 3.1 resolver consults this, so a registered-but-deleted offline file already falls through to a fresh stream URL AT RESOLVE TIME. The "dangling file:// at build/resolve time" case is therefore handled by 3.1.

REMAINING GAP THIS BEAD CLOSES (reactive failures fileExists cannot catch)
Engine load can still fail AFTER a URL is resolved:
  (a) offline file exists on disk but is corrupt/truncated/unreadable -> AVAudioPlayer load throws;
  (b) file deleted in the race window between resolve and engine.load;
  (c) the resolved stream URL itself fails to load (token edge, transient).
In all three, CrossfadeEngine.play -> activeSlot.load throws (CrossfadeEngine.swift:61-67) -> transitionToError sets playbackState=.error(message) (406-412). QueueManager.handleEngineStateChange (QueueManager.swift:375-403) only reacts to .idle (advance) and trackID sync — it IGNORES .error. Result: playback dead-ends with no recovery. That is this bug.

IMPORTANT ENGINE QUIRK: on a failed play(), CrossfadeEngine sets currentTrackID only on success (line 76), and transitionToError does NOT reset it. So engine.currentTrackID is unreliable for identifying which item failed. Recovery MUST key off QueueManager.currentItem (its own currentIndex), not engine.currentTrackID.

DESIGN

1) Resolver gains an offline-skip mode — Lunara/Music/Queue/PlaybackURLResolver.swift (created in 3.1)
   Change signature to: func resolvePlaybackURL(for item: QueueItem, allowOffline: Bool) async throws -> URL.
   allowOffline=true (default call site behavior): current 3.1 logic (offline-then-stream).
   allowOffline=false: SKIP the offline branch entirely, return try await library.streamURL(forKey: item.streamKey). Needed so the retry doesn't just re-pick the same bad offline file (case (a), where fileExists still passes).
   Update the 3.1 call sites in QueueManager.playCurrentItem / prepareNextTrackIfNeeded to pass allowOffline: true.

2) QueueManager reactive recovery — Lunara/Music/Queue/QueueManager.swift
   Add state: private var streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID: String? (guards against infinite retry loops).
   In handleEngineStateChange, add an .error branch (before/after the existing .idle check): if engine.playbackState.hasError, let item = currentItem, and streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID != item.trackID -> set streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID = item.trackID and call a new recoverCurrentItemViaStream(). If streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID == item.trackID (stream retry ALSO failed) -> stop retrying: set lastError = .playbackFailed/streamFailed and leave the error surfaced (do NOT loop, do NOT silently advance).
   recoverCurrentItemViaStream(): re-resolve currentItem with allowOffline:false, then engine.play(url: streamURL, trackID:), preserving position via pendingSeekAfterNextPlay = lastPersistedElapsed (so a mid-track failure resumes near where it died). Mirror the Task/MainActor + signalBuffering pattern already in playCurrentItem (since a stream URL is remote -> runs through TrackCache path). On resolver throw here, set lastError and stop.
   Clear streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID whenever a DIFFERENT track starts successfully (e.g. in syncCurrentIndexToEngineTrack and advanceAndPlayNextIfPossible / at the top of a successful playCurrentItem) so each track gets one fresh recovery attempt.

3) Consider routing the recovery through playCurrentItem with an internal "forceStream" flag instead of a separate method, to avoid duplicating the TrackCache/seek/persist block. Implementer's choice; keep it DRY.

EDGE CASES / NOTES
- Loop guard is essential: offline-corrupt -> error -> stream retry -> stream also errors must terminate, not ping-pong.
- handleEngineStateChange currently early-returns during manualNavigationTargetTrackID suppression (378-384); make sure the .error branch isn't swallowed when a manual nav target is set and the target track fails to load — likely want recovery to still fire for the manual target.
- prepareNext (crossfade next-track) dead-file failures are logged-and-skipped today (CrossfadeEngine.swift:184-194); leaving next-track recovery OUT OF SCOPE is acceptable — the failed next track will just re-resolve when it becomes current. Note this explicitly; do not gold-plate.

TESTING (Swift Testing; iPhone 17 Pro OS:26.2). Failing first, show red.
   - PlaybackURLResolver: allowOffline:false returns a stream URL even when an offline file IS present for the trackID.
   - QueueManager: engine enters .error while playing current item -> QueueManager re-resolves with allowOffline:false and calls engine.play with the stream URL (use a mock engine that records play() calls + a mock resolver).
   - QueueManager: stream retry ALSO errors -> no second re-resolve (loop guard holds), lastError is set.
   - QueueManager: streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID resets when a different track begins (so a later failure on another track still recovers).
   - QueueManager: recovery preserves position (pendingSeekAfterNextPlay == lastPersistedElapsed at retry).
acceptance_criteria:
- When the engine fails to load the current item (corrupt offline file, file deleted post-resolve, or stream load failure), QueueManager automatically re-resolves forcing a stream and retries playback once.
- The retry does NOT reuse the failed offline file (resolver allowOffline:false path).
- If the stream retry also fails, playback stops with a surfaced lastError and does NOT loop infinitely.
- Recovery keys off QueueManager.currentItem, not engine.currentTrackID.
- Each distinct track gets exactly one recovery attempt (guard resets on new track).
- Mid-track failures resume near the prior playback position.
- prepareNext/crossfade next-track failures remain logged-and-skipped (explicitly out of scope).
- Full test suite green on iPhone 17 Pro OS:26.2.
notes: Implemented reactive stream recovery (#60 lazy-resolver seam). Resolver gained allowOffline:; QueueManager .error branch (top of handleEngineStateChange, above manual-nav guard) re-resolves forcing stream once per track, guarded by streamRecoveryAttemptedTrackID + lastPlayedURLWasFile, resumes via pendingSeekAfterNextPlay=lastPersistedElapsed. Also: failed play now skips persist/prepareNext (was clobbering lastError via persist-success clear). Crossfade-advanced failures stay out of scope (lastPlayedURLWasFile reset in syncCurrentIndexToEngineTrack). 9 new tests (8 QueueManager + 1 resolver). Full suite green on iPhone 17 Pro OS 26.4.1. Pending: commit + push.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #61 (squash-merged to main). Reactive stream recovery: resolver allowOffline, QueueManager .error branch with per-track guard, position-preserving single retry. 9 tests, full suite green.

title: Queue persists stable track IDs, not resolved URLs
description: QueueManager.swift:296 bakes URLs at build time; breaks after download/delete.
design:
SCOPE: This bead is being executed TOGETHER WITH Lunara-uww.3.2 (lazy URL resolution). They are inseparable — the moment QueueItem stops carrying a baked URL, the play path has nothing to play, which is exactly what 3.2 fills in. One PR closes both. Decisions confirmed with maintainer 2026-06-05: (1) combine 3.1+3.2; (2) store stable Plex stream key in QueueItem (no Track re-fetch at play time).

ROOT CAUSE
QueueItem carries `url: URL` (Lunara/Music/Queue/QueueManagerProtocol.swift:6). It is resolved once at queue-build time in AppRouter.resolveQueueItemsConcurrently / queueItem(for:) (Lunara/Router/AppRouter.swift:266-331) and that resolved URL is persisted in QueueSnapshot. QueueManager.playCurrentItem (QueueManager.swift:174-213) and prepareNextTrackIfNeeded (227-266) read currentItem.url directly. Consequences after enqueue: a track downloaded later keeps replaying the remote stream; a deleted offline file replays a dead file:// URL; a persisted stream URL carries an expired X-Plex-Token across launches.

streamURL(forTrack:) (Lunara/Library/API/PlexAPIClient.swift:134-147) only uses track.key + a fresh token. So track.key is the single stable input needed to rebuild a stream URL at play time — store it, don't re-fetch the Track.

DESIGN

1) Model — Lunara/Music/Queue/QueueManagerProtocol.swift
   QueueItem: replace `let url: URL` with `let streamKey: String` (= Plex track.key). Keep trackID (plexID), albumID, trackNumber. Update init. Persisted QueueSnapshot now holds stable identifiers only. NOTE: this changes the on-disk Codable shape — old persisted queues will fail to decode. FileQueueStatePersistence.load() already catches decode errors and QueueManager.restorePersistedQueue handles a throw by clearing to empty (QueueManager.swift:316-322), so a one-time queue reset on upgrade is acceptable. Confirm no migration is wanted (default: none).

2) Stream-URL-from-key primitive
   - Lunara/Library/API/PlexAPIClient.swift: add `func streamURL(forKey key: String) async throws -> URL` containing the components/token build currently in streamURL(forTrack:); make streamURL(forTrack:) call streamURL(forKey: track.key).
   - Lunara/Library/Repo/LibraryRepoProtocol.swift + LibraryRepo.swift: surface `streamURL(forKey:)` through the repo protocol (delegates to remote), mirroring the existing streamURL(for:) plumbing (LibraryRepo.swift:215-218, LibraryRepoProtocol.swift:86/226).

3) Resolver (new) — Lunara/Music/Queue/PlaybackURLResolver.swift
   protocol PlaybackURLResolving: Sendable { func resolvePlaybackURL(for item: QueueItem) async throws -> URL }
   Concrete impl holds offlineStore (OfflineStoreProtocol?) + library (LibraryRepoProtocol). Logic: if let offlineStore, let localURL = try await offlineStore.localFileURL(forTrackID: item.trackID) { return localURL } else { return try await library.streamURL(forKey: item.streamKey) }. This is AppRouter.resolveURL (AppRouter.swift:24-30) re-homed to operate on a QueueItem instead of a Track.

4) QueueManager — Lunara/Music/Queue/QueueManager.swift
   Add optional `resolver: PlaybackURLResolving?` (same optional-injection pattern as trackCache/loudnessProvider, init lines 36-48). In playCurrentItem (171-214): resolve the URL via resolver at play time, THEN keep the existing isFileURL-vs-TrackCache branch on the resolved URL (file/local -> engine.play directly; remote -> signalBuffering + trackCache.prepare). Wrap in the existing Task; on resolver throw, set lastError and bail (do NOT play a stale URL). prepareNextTrackIfNeeded (216-273): resolve nextItem URL the same way before the isFileURL branch. If resolver is nil (tests that don't inject one), preserve current behavior is impossible since url is gone — tests must inject a resolver mock (see tests).

5) Wiring — Lunara/App/AppCoordinator.swift
   offlineStore is currently built AFTER queueManager (104-117). Reorder: build offlineStore + offlineDirectory first, then construct the resolver (offlineStore + libraryRepo), then pass resolver into QueueManager(...). AppRouter still receives offlineStore as today (122).

6) Builders — Lunara/Router/AppRouter.swift
   Stop resolving URLs at build time. resolveQueueItemsConcurrently (266-291) and queueItem(for:) (320-331) emit QueueItem(trackID: track.plexID, streamKey: track.key, albumID: track.albumID, trackNumber: track.trackNumber). Delete resolveURL (24-30) and the per-item URL resolution inside the task group. Builders no longer need offlineStore for URL purposes (verify no other use before removing).

TESTING (Swift Testing; iPhone 17 Pro OS:26.2). Write failing first, show red.
   - QueueStatePersistenceTests: round-trip stores/restores streamKey, no url field present. Update existing QueueItem(...url:...) literals (lines ~23,24,51).
   - QueueManagerTests: inject a PlaybackURLResolving mock. (a) playCurrentItem calls resolver and plays the resolved URL; (b) download-after-enqueue: resolver returns file:// the second time -> engine plays local; (c) resolver throw -> lastError set, engine NOT asked to play a stale URL. Update all QueueItem(...url:...) literals (lines 186-209+ and elsewhere).
   - NowPlayingScreenViewModelTests, AppRouterTests, AppCoordinatorTests: update QueueItem constructions to streamKey.
   - AppRouterTests: builders emit streamKey from track.key and no longer call streamURL at build time.

OUT OF SCOPE (separate beads): 3.4 graceful fallback when offline file:// missing -> re-resolve to stream (resolver makes this trivial later); 3.6 re-resolve queue on download complete/remove; 3.5 unify OfflineStore+TrackCache.
acceptance_criteria:
- QueueItem no longer has a `url` field; carries trackID + streamKey + albumID + trackNumber.
- Persisted QueueSnapshot contains no resolved URLs (stable IDs only); round-trip test passes.
- URL is resolved at PLAY time via PlaybackURLResolving: offline file if present, else fresh stream URL from streamKey.
- Track downloaded AFTER enqueue plays the local file on next play without rebuilding the queue (test).
- Resolver failure sets lastError and does not play a stale URL (test).
- LibraryRepoProtocol exposes streamURL(forKey:); streamURL(forTrack:) delegates to it.
- AppRouter builders no longer resolve URLs at build time.
- Full test suite green on iPhone 17 Pro OS:26.2.
notes: Folds in Lunara-uww.3.2 (close both together). Maintainer decisions 2026-06-05: combine 3.1+3.2; store streamKey in QueueItem (no Track re-fetch). Open micro-decision left to implementer: no on-disk migration for old persisted queues (one-time reset on upgrade is acceptable since restore already clears on decode error).
close_reason: Already shipped in commit bd2021b (#60): QueueItem carries streamKey, PlaybackURLResolver resolves lazily at play time, wired in AppCoordinator. Beads were stale/open.

title: BUG: AlbumMarquee blows up the collection page layout (intrinsic width leaks into ScrollView)
description: Device screenshot 2026-06-11: collections view broken after Lunara-1mu — no play/shuffle buttons visible, grid cards bleeding off both edges, marquee tiles oversized. Cause: rowContent applies .fixedSize(horizontal: true) to the 2x-duplicated tile strip (~16 tiles ≈ 1300pt) IN the layout hierarchy, so the header reports that as its ideal width; the ScrollView content adopts it and the visible screen shows the center slice — title/buttons end up offscreen-left, grid lays out at ~3x screen width. Fix: render the strip as an .overlay(alignment: .leading) on a Color.clear base sized maxWidth/.infinity x tileSize, then clip — overlay content never affects parent layout. Regression test: ImageRenderer ideal-width probe stays near screen width.
close_reason: Tile strip now renders as .overlay(alignment: .leading) on a Color.clear base (maxWidth infinity x tileSize) and is clipped — overlay content never participates in parent layout, so the strip's ~1300pt width can't leak into the ScrollView. Regression test: ImageRenderer ideal-width probe was 1256pt before the fix, <=400 after. Title/buttons and the album grid return to normal screen-width layout.

title: BUG: paused playback spontaneously resumes (interruption-ended auto-resume fires over a deliberate pause)
description: Repro (Tim, 2026-06-11): pause music; later it starts playing by itself. ROOT CAUSE FOUND: CrossfadeEngine.wireInterruptions marks ANY interruptionBegan as an interruption-initiated pause — even when playback was already deliberately paused. A later interruptionEnded(shouldResume: true) then passes the Lunara-gf5 guard (wasInterrupted=true, state=.paused) and auto-resumes. Any Siri invocation, phone call, alarm, or another app briefly taking audio focus while Lunara sits paused triggers it. FIX: onInterruptionBegan only sets pausedByInterruption when playbackState == .playing (a paused app has nothing to interrupt). Plus telemetry: interruption phase records and remote-command records so any remaining rogue resume (e.g. Bluetooth devices sending play on connect) is visible in the exported log.
close_reason: Root cause: onInterruptionBegan marked ANY interruption as an interruption-pause, including ones arriving while the user was already deliberately paused — so interruptionEnded(shouldResume) auto-resumed over the user's pause (Siri/calls/other apps taking focus trigger this). Fix: interruptionBegan only sets pausedByInterruption when playbackState == .playing. Tests: user-paused interruption cycle stays paused (red before: was .playing); active-playback interruption still auto-resumes. Instrumentation: 'interruption' phase/resumed records + 'remoteCommand' play/pause/next/previous records in the bridge, so any remaining rogue resume on device (e.g. Bluetooth play-on-connect) shows up attributed in the telemetry export.

title: BUG: CrossfadePolicy is fed the NEXT track's loudness as the OUTGOING track's contour
description: QueueManager.prepareNextTrackIfNeeded (QueueManager.swift:298) fetches loudnessProvider.fetchLoudnessLevels(trackID: nextItem.trackID) and passes it to CrossfadePolicy.transition as loudnessLevels, but the policy uses those levels with currentTrackDuration to detect the fade-out onset at the END of the OUTGOING track (CrossfadePolicy.swift:49-91, walks backwards from the array end). So every shuffle crossfade decision is computed from the wrong track's contour — the outro detection, fade duration, and start time are essentially random with respect to the song that's actually ending. Fix: fetch loudness for currentItem.trackID (the track that will fade out). Keep fetching next's levels too once fade-in onset lands (see smart-fades bead).
acceptance_criteria: CrossfadePolicy receives the outgoing track's loudness contour; unit test proves the trackID requested from the loudness provider matches the currently playing item, not the staged next item.

description: One @MainActor @Observable resolver owns a bounded LRU keyed by trackID of {track, album, artist, full-size UIImage, thumbnail UIImage, palette, loudness}. Unblocks 7.2/7.3.

title: Now Playing performance: shared metadata resolution + responsive lock screen
description:
Strategic perf epic. Root finding (read-only investigation, all cited): the Now Playing lag is NOT network latency — library.track/album/artist/URL lookups are local GRDB SQLite (sub-ms; LibraryStore.swift:38-68, PlexAPIClient URL building is pure string work). The lag is redundant, sequential, MainActor-bound resolution across THREE uncoordinated consumers that each independently resolve the same track + artwork on every change, plus the lock screen keying off the engine's late currentTrackID.

DUPLICATION per single track change: library.track resolved 3x, library.album 3x, full-size artwork fetch+decode 2x (NowPlayingScreenViewModel.swift:175-280, NowPlayingBarViewModel.swift:126-159, NowPlayingBridge.swift:151-221), plus Up Next re-resolves all 20 rows serially (4 calls + decode each) on EVERY queue change (NowPlayingScreenViewModel.swift:351-405; dedup removed in rhp). No shared cache; all sequential awaits ping-ponging through the main actor.

ALREADY GOOD (do not redo): disk artwork LRU cache (ArtworkPipeline.swift:142-176); all decode/downsample off-main via Task.detached; loudnessCache memoization; in-app two-phase apply (text+clear, then artwork) on the screen; snapshotCache+prefetch for the main path.

GOAL: one shared cached resolver feeding all consumers; lock screen updates in lockstep with the in-app UI; Up Next windowed/incremental. Targets Lunara-wtj (lock-screen ~10s lag) and Lunara-uww.3.9 (stale art + lag on replace) together with general lag.
close_reason: All 8 children closed: shared resolver (7.1), windowed Up Next (7.2), decoded-image caches (7.3), parallel resolution (7.4), timeout/retry tuning (7.5), artwork-first apply (7.6), lock-screen lag fix (wtj), scrobbler routing (0hp).

title: Lock-screen Now Playing metadata lags ~10s behind track change (remote next command)
description:
REPRO (on device): On the lock screen, tap Next. Audio advances to the next song immediately (good), but the lock-screen metadata (title/artist/artwork) keeps showing the PREVIOUS track for ~10s before updating.

LIKELY AREA: NowPlayingBridge updates MPNowPlayingInfoCenter.nowPlayingInfo when currentTrackID/playbackState/queue.currentIndex change (NowPlayingBridge.swift:108-114). The ~10s suggests the new track's metadata resolution (library.track / album / artwork fetch) is slow and nowPlayingInfo isn't published with text immediately + artwork-when-ready. Investigate: does the bridge resolve metadata synchronously/awaited before publishing anything? Apply the same two-phase pattern used in NowPlayingScreenViewModel (#70): publish text immediately on track change, attach artwork when it resolves. Also check whether a network timeout/retry is causing the 10s specifically.

ACCEPTANCE: lock-screen title/artist update within ~1s of a remote next/prev; artwork follows as soon as it resolves.
design:
ROOT CAUSE (investigation, cited): NowPlayingBridge observes engine.currentTrackID (NowPlayingBridge.swift:93,109), which CrossfadeEngine sets only AFTER the stream URL is resolved and the audio file is loaded (CrossfadeEngine.swift:120,416,461). On a remote next/prev the queue index changes immediately but engine.currentTrackID lags by resolve+load time — so the lock screen waits while the in-app screen/bar (which observe queueManager.currentItem) update promptly. Secondary: publishMetadata gates nowPlayingInfo behind awaited library.track + library.album (NowPlayingBridge.swift:159,172,190) and artwork behind a 30s timeout + backoff retries.

FIX: observe queueManager.currentItem (not engine.currentTrackID); publish text-only nowPlayingInfo immediately on currentItem change, then patch artwork/elapsed when the engine confirms the track. Best built on the shared resolver (Lunara-uww.7.1). Also relax applyArtwork's engine.currentTrackID guard (NowPlayingBridge.swift:224) so lock-screen art isn't pinned to the late engine signal.
close_reason: Fixed + verified on device (PR #81): lock-screen metadata now follows the queue promptly; bridge no longer blocks on artwork fetch. 5 new tests; full suite green.

title: Lunara not engaging system audio: no lock-screen Now Playing, doesn't interrupt other apps (ducks instead)
description:
SYMPTOMS (on device):
1. Lock screen shows no Now Playing controls/metadata for Lunara (Plexamp does show them).
2. Hitting Play in Lunara while Plexamp is playing does NOT take over — Plexamp keeps playing underneath; Lunara plays on top.

LEADS:
- AudioSession.swift:62 configures the session as '.playback, mode: .default, options: [.duckOthers]'. '.duckOthers' lowers other audio but lets it CONTINUE — that explains Plexamp playing underneath. To take over, drop '.duckOthers' (plain '.playback' interrupts non-mixable audio and makes Lunara the active 'now playing' app).
- NowPlayingBridge.swift exists (MPNowPlayingInfoCenter / MPRemoteCommandCenter). Verify it is actually instantiated/retained and fed: that the bridge populates MPNowPlayingInfoCenter.nowPlayingInfo (title/artist/artwork/duration/elapsed/rate), registers MPRemoteCommandCenter handlers (play/pause/next/prev), and that AVAudioSession is setActive(true) BEFORE playback so the lock screen binds to Lunara. The two symptoms likely share a root cause: the session never becomes the active playing session.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Lock screen + Control Center show Lunara metadata (art/title/artist) and working transport controls.
- Starting Lunara playback interrupts/stops other apps' audio (Plexamp pauses), not ducks-and-continues.
close_reason: Fixed + verified on device: dropped .duckOthers from .playback category (AudioSession.swift:62) so Lunara interrupts other audio and claims the Now Playing slot. Merged in PR #76.

title: Up Next list stale after queue replace (shuffle new artist) until track advances
description:
REPRO: Queue has artist A's songs. Shuffle artist B (e.g. Weird Al) -> main metadata updates to B correctly, but the Up Next list keeps showing artist A's tracks. It only refreshes when currentIndex changes (track advances naturally or manual skip). Confirmed on device via screenshot (playing Weird Al 'Inactive', Up Next still showing prior queue).

ROOT CAUSE: NowPlayingScreenViewModel.resolveUpNextIfNeeded() dedups on (currentIndex, items.count). A full queue replacement via playNow resets currentIndex=0; if the new queue has the same item count, the guard sees no change and skips re-resolving Up Next. Main metadata escapes the bug because handleCurrentItemChange keys on trackID.

FIX: Delete the (index,count) dedup guard. reconcile() never reassigns an identical items array (early-returns unless it removed tracks), and every other queue mutation is a genuine change, so the guard prevents no real redundant work -- it only causes this staleness. resolveUpNextIfNeeded becomes: cancel in-flight upNextTask, start fresh resolution (already cancellation-safe).

Distinct from Lunara-2jb (end-of-track title/waveform staleness).
close_reason: Fixed: removed the (index,count) dedup guard in NowPlayingScreenViewModel.resolveUpNextIfNeeded so a full queue replace (shuffle new artist) refreshes Up Next. Test upNextRefreshesWhenQueueReplacedWithSameCountAndIndex green; verified on device.

title: Now Playing: stale artwork + lag on queue replace (MainActor image work)
description: User repro: launch with a previously-enqueued (restored) queue, tap Shuffle <Artist>. Now Playing shows the PREVIOUS queue's metadata+artwork for a considerable time before updating; general lag; lots of caching-log activity while idle on Now Playing. Root cause (staff-reviewed): NowPlayingScreenViewModel gates the WHOLE display on the slowest awaited element (full-size artwork network fetch) before clearing stale UI, and does CPU-heavy image decode + palette extraction + 20x up-next downsample synchronously on the MainActor, starving current-track resolution.
design: Fix: (1) two-phase apply — show new text immediately and CLEAR previous artwork/palette/waveform, apply artwork when ready (user wants no old-art-with-new-text); (2) offload decode + palette + up-next downsample via Task.detached (precedent NowPlayingBridge:212); (3) run up-next + prefetch at .utility to remove priority inversion; (4) ArtworkPaletteTheme: Sendable. title: Research excessive artwork downloading in library grid (full-res 'thumbnails', possible cache thrash)
description: Observed during manual testing (2026-06-07): browsing the library grid emits a continuous flood of 'artwork DOWNLOAD ... STORED' logs (ArtworkPipeline.swift:81,99) — hundreds of album thumbnails fetched in sequence. The pipeline DOES cache (cachedFileURL checked first, fetchArtwork ArtworkPipeline.swift:68-99), so every one of these is a cache MISS. User intuition: 'we cache images all the time and they're similar images.' Investigate and quantify before fixing.
design:
HYPOTHESES to test:
1. THUMBNAILS ARE FULL-RES. Stored sizes range to ~10MB (e.g. album/97842 = 9924 KB; 75424 = 2200 KB; 97791 = 2325 KB) for grid cells that render ~200-400px. Likely requesting the raw Plex art URL instead of /photo/:/transcode?width=&height=. Check where the thumbnail sourceURL is built (Album/Artist/Collection models + LibraryRepo+AlbumMetadata) — is it a scaled transcode or the original?
2. CACHE THRASH. enforceCacheLimit (ArtworkPipeline.swift:153-176) is LRU by total size; if the cap is small relative to a large library, browsing evicts and re-downloads -> 'downloading all the time'. Check the configured limit vs typical library art volume.
3. CACHE-KEY CHURN. fileName(for:sourceURL:) (ArtworkPipeline.swift:221) keys on sourceURL; if the URL carries a volatile token/param, keys never match -> permanent misses. Verify the sourceURL is stable across launches.
4. EAGER/UNWINDOWED PREFETCH. Pagination landed (Lunara-uww.4.1 keyset cursors) but artwork prefetch may not be windowed to visible cells -> whole-library fetch on browse.
EVIDENCE: ArtworkPipeline.swift:68-99 (fetch path + logs), :153-176 (eviction), :221 (cache key).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause(s) identified with evidence; a recommendation (transcoded thumbnails / windowed prefetch / cache sizing) written up; follow-up fix bead(s) filed.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #72: transcoded thumbnails via Plex /photo/:/transcode (600px) across all 13 thumbnail call sites + one-shot launch cache invalidation.

title: Now Playing UI doesn't update when track auto-advances at end-of-track
description:
REPRO: Artist page (Mumford & Sons) -> Shuffle -> Now Playing screen opens, plays 'Little Lion Man' (correct). When the track ENDS, audio advances to the next track (audible, correct) BUT the Now Playing UI does NOT update: still shows old track title + same waveform/visualizer. The animated playhead resets to start (white) but it's the SAME waveform/metadata as the previous track, not the new one.

SYMPTOMS:
- Engine + audio advance correctly; only the Now Playing VIEW is stale.
- Playhead resets but waveform/title do not refresh to the new track.
- Also observed: UI was 'extremely laggy / not buttery smooth' during playback (separate perf concern; may be debug build or main-thread work — note but verify).

LIKELY AREA (engine auto-advance -> QueueManager sync -> NowPlaying VM observation):
- CrossfadeEngine.handleTrackEnded() swaps slots, plays next, sets currentTrackID = new track (Lunara/Music/Engine/CrossfadeEngine.swift ~343).
- QueueManager.observeEngineState/handleEngineStateChange -> syncCurrentIndexToEngineTrack advances currentIndex only if items[currentIndex+1].trackID == engineTrackID (QueueManager.swift ~395/440).
- NowPlayingScreenViewModel: determine whether it observes queueManager.currentIndex/currentItem or a snapshot cache keyed by trackID; suspected the view isn't reacting to the advance, OR the snapshot for the new track is missing/stale so it falls back to the old one. Snapshot cache eviction lives ~NowPlayingScreenViewModel:270-291.

RESEARCH GOAL: pin whether the break is (a) QueueManager not advancing currentIndex on natural end-of-track, or (b) NowPlaying VM/view not reacting to the advance / snapshot selection stale. Then propose fix.

NOTE: Found while collecting telemetry (Lunara-w4v); telemetry log from the session will show the engine handleTrackEnded->play event with the new trackID, confirming the engine advanced. Not caused by telemetry (engine emit calls are additive). Likely pre-existing, surfaced by playing through a track end.

title: Re-resolve queue when downloads complete or are removed
description: syncCollection/removeDownload should signal queue (DownloadManager.swift:91).
design:
Core bug: download remove/complete emit NO signal to the queue (DownloadManager.swift:88 just sets albumStates). Crossfade pre-resolves the NEXT item and preloads its URL into CrossfadeEngine (QueueManager.swift:287-296). 3.4 graceful fallback only covers the CURRENT-item resolve path (playCurrentItem), NOT the preloaded next-track buffer.

Consequences:
- Remove download for an Up-Next track -> CrossfadeEngine holds a dangling file:// -> crossfades into silence/failure. (correctness bug)
- Download completes for an Up-Next streaming track -> keeps streaming instead of switching to offline file. (cosmetic)

Plan:
1. DownloadManager: after deleteOfflineTracks (removeDownload, :87) and after album download completes, emit a signal carrying changed albumID(s). Mechanism TBD vs existing patterns (@Observable field vs async callback/Combine).
2. QueueManager: observe signal; if a changed albumID matches the pre-resolved next item, cancel prepareNextTask + invalidate preloaded buffer and re-run prepareNextTrackIfNeeded(). Optionally re-resolve current if it matches.
3. Tests-first in LunaraTests/: (a) removing download for Up-Next track invalidates/re-resolves preload; (b) completing download for Up-Next streaming track re-resolves to offline.
close_reason: Merged to main in PR #68 (commit 2463783). 10 tests, 415/415 green.

title: Collection marquee only samples the first 12 albums — large collections repeat the same covers
description: Screenshot 2026-06-11 3:01PM (Albums from 2024, 63 albums): header marquee cycles the same ~8 covers with visible repeats. ROOT CAUSE (researched, not fixed): CollectionDetailView.marqueeThumbnailURLs = viewModel.albums.prefix(12) and the thumbnail loader loop also only resolves prefix(12) (CollectionDetailView.swift:117,126). Even/odd split puts ~6 per row, then AlbumMarquee.paddedURLs repeats them up to tilesPerRowMinimum=8 — so a 63-album collection shows 12 covers max with in-row repetition. FIX DIRECTION: widen and diversify the sample — e.g. take up to ~32 albums sampled across the WHOLE collection (stride or seeded shuffle for variety) instead of the first 12; eagerly resolve those thumbnails async (AlbumMarquee already renders nil as placeholder tiles and picks up URLs as they land; tiles decode small via DownsampledThumbnail at ~tileSize*3 px so cost is bounded; most thumbs are already disk-cached from sync per README). Keep a cap (32ish) so a 239-album collection ('The Key Albums') does not fetch everything for a decorative header. Avoid duplicate covers within a row when the pool allows (dedupe before paddedURLs). ACCEPTANCE: open a 60+ album collection — both marquee rows show varied artwork from across the collection, no visible repeats while watching for ~30s; small collections (<8) still pad/repeat gracefully as today.
notes: Origin: QA step 10. Cheap fix; pairs visually with the cold-cache skeleton check (uwc) on the same screen. TIM'S ADDED ACCEPTANCE (2026-06-11): when the collection has enough albums (>~12), NO repeated cover should be visible ON SCREEN AT ONCE — across BOTH rows combined, not just within a row. Implementation note: visible tiles ≈ 5-6 per row at 150pt header (tile ~71pt) → need ~12+ distinct covers minimum; partition the sampled pool DISJOINTLY between rows (no cover in both rows), keep the doubled strip (urls+urls) for wrap but ensure pool-per-row ≥ tiles-visible+1 so the wrap seam never shows a duplicate next to itself; only fall back to repetition when the collection genuinely has fewer covers than needed.

title: Investigate: butter-smooth album grid scrolling (sluggish + UI hang scrolling deep into 2,000+ albums)
description: Device QA 2026-06-11 step 9: scrolling the Albums grid toward 'D' got increasingly sluggish, then the app HUNG (not a crash — no crash log expected). INVESTIGATION bead: profile + fix-list, implementation in child beads. CONTEXT (already researched): album metadata IS cached in GRDB and pages load locally (LibraryGridViewModel pageSize=50, trigger ~10 cards from end), so reaching 'D' in a 2,000+ library means dozens of serial page-appends while scrolling. PRIME SUSPECTS, in order: (1) LibraryGridViewModel.thumbnailURL(for:) is called from every cell's BODY and calls touchArtwork -> artworkLRU.removeAll (O(300) linear scan) AND mutates stored state during view rendering; artworkLRU is a tracked @Observable property (no @ObservationIgnored), so body-time mutation can trigger invalidation storms / 'modifying state during view update' — classic SwiftUI hang shape. Fix candidates: @ObservationIgnored on artworkLRU + move LRU touch out of the read path. (2) artworkByAlbumID is one observable dictionary read by ALL visible cells — every thumbnail arrival invalidates every visible cell (property-level tracking, not key-level); during fast scroll that is a re-render storm multiplying suspect 1. (3) DownsampledThumbnail re-decodes from disk on each appearance (maxPixelSize 540, decode bounded per Lunara-gxq but repeated); consider an NSCache of decoded UIImages. (4) Serial 50-row page-appends: each append rebuilds filteredAlbums and grows the LazyVGrid ForEach; consider larger pages, prefetch-ahead, or just loading all ~2,000 Album rows up front (structs are tiny; paging the GRID may be unnecessary even though paging the DB read is cheap). (5) Two .task modifiers per cell (pagination probe + artwork) — overhead per cell churn. METHOD: reproduce in sim with library, Instruments (SwiftUI body counts, Hangs, Time Profiler), confirm suspect 1 first since it is cheap to fix and likely dominant. ALSO CONSIDER (UX, may spin off): A-Z section index/scrubber so reaching 'D' does not require traversing hundreds of cells. ACCEPTANCE for the eventual fixes: full-speed scroll top-to-bottom with no hang, no visible hitching, memory flat.
notes: Related: Lunara-uww.4.2 (LRU cap) and Lunara-gxq (bounded decode) addressed memory, not render-path CPU. The hang is new evidence pointing at body-time state mutation rather than memory. Pairs with the sort bead (Lunara sort options) — sort must not break pagination cursors.

title: Radar qualifying artists built from Plex critic rating, not the user's star rating
description: Device QA 2026-06-11: radar surfaced Bloc Party, whom Tim has NOT rated 4.5★+. Backfill happens naturally on next library refresh; radar artist_mbids cache unaffected. ACCEPTANCE: radar only sweeps artists with a genuinely user-rated 4.5★+ album; Bloc Party gone unless Tim rates them.

REFERENCE (how it works today, for the bead reader): refresh kicks off when RadarView opens via .task -> loadCached() then refreshIfStale(); gated to once per 3 days via UserDefaults 'radar.lastCheck'; one MB artist-search + release-group fetch per rated artist at the client's 1 req/s throttle (~2s/artist, so ~50 artists = ~2 min); results persist to GRDB radar_entries and publish when the WHOLE sweep finishes — switching to publish-as-you-go is part of this bead.

title: Investigate: incremental sync purges album_collections junction rows (root of slow collection opens + 5dh trigger)
description: LibraryStore+IncrementalSync.swift:96 runs DELETE FROM album_collections WHERE lastSeenSyncID IS NULL OR lastSeenSyncID != ? at completeIncrementalSync. If a sync run doesn't re-stamp membership rows for UNCHANGED albums/collections, this wipes valid junction rows — leaving collections with empty local membership. That emptiness (a) forced a remote fetch on every collection open (now mitigated by wd4's writeback, but the writeback rows carry NULL lastSeenSyncID and will be purged again by the next incremental sync) and (b) was the likely trigger for the 5dh mass-delete (now fail-safe, but the data loss vector in the junction remains). Verify the re-stamping behavior in relationship reconciliation; if unchanged rows aren't re-stamped, either stamp them or scope the purge to collections actually visited by the run.
close_reason: CONFIRMED then fixed: upsertAlbumCollections had ZERO callers — refreshLibrary never fetched or stamped collection membership, so pruneRowsNotSeen wiped the entire album_collections junction on EVERY refresh. That made every collection open hit the network (pre-wd4) and emptied the ownership data the 5dh removal guard depended on. Fix: refreshLibrary now fetches membership per remote collection (per-collection failures logged and skipped, never destructive) and stamps it via upsertAlbumCollections before the prune — junction rows survive refreshes, wd4's NULL-stamped writeback rows get re-stamped naturally next refresh. Test: refreshLibrary_stampsCollectionMembershipForTheRun (red: zero fetches, nothing stamped).

title: Downloads page: queued album shows Plex ID / 'Unknown Artist' until first track downloads
description:
On DownloadsView, when an album is newly queued, the Downloading row shows the raw Plex album ID as the title and 'Unknown Artist' as the subtitle until the first track finishes downloading (see user screenshot: '72008 / Unknown Artist 0/11').

ROOT CAUSE (scoped, not implemented):
- DownloadsView.activeSection (Lunara/Views/Settings/DownloadsView.swift:31-47) resolves the row's Album via album(for:) which only searches viewModel.downloadedAlbums — empty for a brand-new album until its first track is offline AND the 3s polling loop refreshes.
- Fallback title comes from SettingsViewModel.activeDownloadAlbumNames (SettingsViewModel.swift:147-157), which is populated lazily in load() and in observeDownloadProgress()'s 3-second polling tick — so up to ~3s the raw albumID shows.
- The fallback only covers the title; the artist line is hardcoded to album?.artistName ?? "Unknown Artist" (DownloadsView.swift:98), so artist stays wrong even after the name resolves.

PROPOSED FIX:
DownloadManager.downloadAlbum(_ album: Album, tracks:) (Lunara/Library/Offline/DownloadManager.swift:63) already receives the full Album — it just discards the metadata. Store it: add private(set) var albumMetadata: [String: Album] (or title+artist tuple) populated when a download is enqueued (also in syncCollection path, line 99, which has the Album too). DownloadsView's activeSection then reads title/artist from that map, with albumID as last-resort fallback. This makes the name available synchronously at enqueue time and lets us delete the polling-based activeDownloadAlbumNames resolution in SettingsViewModel.

FILES: Lunara/Library/Offline/DownloadManager.swift, Lunara/Views/Settings/SettingsViewModel.swift, Lunara/Views/Settings/DownloadsView.swift

title: Stop the 0.25s elapsed UI timer while the app is backgrounded
description: CrossfadeEngine.startElapsedTimer (CrossfadeEngine.swift:278) wakes the CPU 4x/second for the whole play session purely to update the in-app elapsed display. On the lock screen iOS interpolates position itself from rate + timestamp (NowPlayingBridge sets those event-driven), and the in-app UI is invisible — so during backgrounded listening (the dominant mode) this is pure battery waste, hours of pointless wakes. Crossfade trigger/ramp timers are unaffected (DispatchSource with leeway, already background-safe). Also consider widening the 10s queue-persistence timer to 30s + persisting on background transition; same event-driven principle.
acceptance_criteria: With playback running, backgrounding the app stops the 0.25s timer (testable via engine hook); foregrounding resumes UI updates within one tick; lock-screen scrubber still advances correctly on device.
close_reason: CrossfadeEngine.sceneDidChangeActivity (PlaybackEngineProtocol requirement, no-op default): elapsed timer stops on background, resumes (with one resync tick) on foreground only while playing; startElapsedTimer guards on scene activity so background play/resume never arms it. Wired in LunaraApp next to telemetry's scene handler. Saves 4 CPU wakes/sec for entire lock-screen listening sessions. 3 new tests.

title: Plexamp-style sweet fades: outgoing outro + incoming music-onset shape the overlap
description: CrossfadePolicy already detects the OUTGOING outro from its loudness contour and sizes the fade (2-12s, gapless for sequential album tracks — correct scope for shuffle-only smart fades). Two gaps vs Plexamp: (1) it knows nothing about the INCOMING track — a song with a long quiet intro fades in as near-silence, leaving an energy hole; (2) when no outro is detected (abrupt ending) it still chops 3s off a full-loudness ending. DESIGN: fetch BOTH contours in prepareNext (outgoing for outro onset — after Lunara-9x1 — incoming for music onset = first sample >= bodyLevelFraction of ITS OWN body level). Compute overlap so the incoming reaches its body energy roughly when the outgoing crosses ~50% fade: startTime = outroOnset, duration = clamp(outroLength + incomingOnsetLead, 2, 12). No-outro case: shorten fade toward minCrossfadeDuration rather than default 3s (cut less of a hot ending). CONSTRAINT: Plex waveform levels may be normalized per track — use only within-track relative measures, never compare absolute levels across tracks. CONSTRAINT: all math is on two 128-float arrays at prepare time — zero steady-state cost, no extra timers (battery).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: quiet-intro incoming lengthens overlap; hot-ending outgoing shortens fade vs default; sequential album tracks stay gapless; all decisions logged via telemetry (see logging bead).
close_reason: CrossfadePolicy now composes the overlap from both contours, within-track relative measures only: detected outgoing outro -> duration = clamp(outro + incoming onset lead, 2, 12); onset lead = seconds of sub-threshold intro on the incoming (its own body-level baseline), capped 4s; contour-present hot endings cut at the 2s minimum (no early body fade, lead ignored); unknown outgoing contour -> default 3s + lead. QueueItem carries optional duration (old persisted queues decode as nil); prepareNext fetches both contours from the store-backed cache; fadeDecision telemetry gains hadNextContour. 6 new policy tests + 3 retuned to the new hot-ending behavior.

title: Persist loudness contours in GRDB + prefetch during album sync (offline + battery)
description: LibraryRepo.fetchLoudnessLevels (LibraryRepo.swift:261-268) hits the Plex API per track with only an unbounded in-memory cache: every session re-fetches per track change (radio wake each song -> battery), and offline the fetch fails so CrossfadePolicy degrades to the default 3s fade exactly where smart fades matter most (synced, offline listening). Fix: (1) GRDB table track_loudness(trackID PK, levels BLOB ~512B for 128 floats, fetchedAt); repo checks store before network, writes through after fetch. (2) DownloadManager.performDownload prefetches loudness per track during album sync (it is already doing network there). (3) Bound the in-memory layer. ~2k albums x ~10 tracks x 512B = ~10MB worst case on disk, fine.
acceptance_criteria: Second playback session of the same tracks issues zero loudness network requests (test via repo with store seeded); synced albums have loudness rows after download; airplane-mode crossfades of synced tracks still get contour-based fades.
close_reason: GRDB v11 migration track_loudness(trackID PK, levels BLOB, fetchedAt). LibraryStore round-trips [Float] as raw bytes (~512B/track). LibraryRepo: memory(bounded 512) -> store -> network, write-through on network success — repeat sessions and offline playback never hit the radio for contours. DownloadManager prefetches loudness per saved track during album sync. Protocol methods declared as requirements (not just extension members) so dispatch is dynamic. 4 new tests.

title: Shuffle starts on an already-local track when one exists (instant first audio)
description: For unsynced/streamed tracks, first audio waits on TrackCache.prepare doing a FULL file download (TrackCache.swift:25-69; AVAudioPlayer needs a complete local file, so this gate is architectural). On shuffle specifically, position 0 is arbitrary — so after shuffling, if any track in the queue is already playable locally (offline store hit via PlaybackURLResolver, or TrackCache.cachedFile), rotate one such track to position 0 (keep the rest of the order). Synced collections already start instantly; this makes partly-synced and recently-played shuffles start instantly too, and saves the radio burst at tap time. Out of scope: progressive streaming engines.
acceptance_criteria: Shuffling a collection containing at least one offline/cached track always starts audio from local disk (no network on the play path); fully-streamed queues behave as today; sequential (non-shuffle) play order is never altered.
close_reason: AppRouter.preferringLocalLead applied to all 5 shuffle paths: one allOfflineAlbumIDs query + localFileURL verification finds the first shuffled item from a downloaded album and rotates it to position 0 (rest of shuffle order preserved); TrackCache checked for the first 5 items as a recently-streamed fallback. Sequential plays never reorder. Cost independent of queue size. 3 new tests.

title: Batch the collection/artist queue build (one query, not one per album)
description: AppRouter.allQueueItemsForAlbums (AppRouter.swift:243-251) loops albums and awaits library.tracks(forAlbum:) once per album — N sequential GRDB round-trips through the MainActor repo before playNow can run. For a 100+ album collection this serial chain is the first chunk of tap-to-audio latency (and CPU wakes). Fix: add a batched store/repo query (tracks for [albumID] in one SQL IN query, ordered by album+trackNumber) and use it for collection/artist/shuffle-all paths. Battery: fewer wakeups, same data.
acceptance_criteria: Shuffling a large collection issues O(1) track queries instead of O(albums); existing ordering preserved for sequential play paths; tests cover the batched query.
close_reason: LibraryStore.fetchTracks(forAlbums:) — one IN-query ordered within albums. LibraryRepo.tracks(forAlbums:) batches the store read, preserves requested album order, and keeps the per-album remote fallback only for cache-miss albums. AppRouter.allQueueItemsForAlbums uses it — collection/artist/shuffle-all queue builds are O(1) store queries instead of O(albums) serial round-trips. Protocol methods are requirements with looping defaults (dynamic dispatch). 3 new tests.

title: Now Playing full-size artwork: downsample decode + apply art before loudness/artist (kill ~1-2s on play)
description:
REPRO: hit Play on an album -> Now Playing artwork takes ~1-2s to appear even though the image is already cached on disk from browsing.

ROOT CAUSE (investigation, cited): NowPlayingScreenViewModel.buildSnapshot decodes the FULL-RESOLUTION original Plex art via UIImage(data:) (NowPlayingScreenViewModel.swift:258) — authenticatedArtworkURL returns the untranscoded original (PlexAPIClient.swift:155), multi-MB/large. The full-res decode is the dominant cost. It's also gated: the snapshot is applied atomically only AFTER searchArtists + authenticatedArtworkURL + fetchFullSize + decode + palette + fetchLoudnessLevels all complete (sequential awaits, :233-266). The mini-bar is faster because it uses the 600px thumbnail via DownsamplingImageLoader.

FIX (user-chosen): (1) decode the full-size with DownsamplingImageLoader.load(contentsOf:maxPixelSize:1024) instead of full-res UIImage(data:) — matches the bar/grid; (2) apply artwork+palette as soon as decoded, then apply artist+waveform when ready (don't gate art behind loudness/artist); parallelize artist+loudness via async let. Extract resolveArtwork/resolveArtist/resolveLoudness helpers shared by resolveAndApply (incremental apply) and buildSnapshot (prefetch). Expected: ~150-300ms, no quality pop.

Distinct from uww.7.3 (in-mem NSCache, repeated re-decode) and uww.7.1 (shared resolver).
close_reason: Fixed + verified on device (PR #82): hero artwork decodes via DownsamplingImageLoader and applies before loudness/artist; ~1-2s delay gone. 2 new tests; full suite green.

title: Windowed/incremental Up Next resolution (reuse cache, diff instead of full rebuild)
description: resolveUpNextItems (NowPlayingScreenViewModel.swift:351-405) re-resolves all 20 rows serially (track+album+thumbURL+fetchThumbnail+decode each) on EVERY queue change since the rhp dedup removal. Fix: resolve only the first ~5 visible rows eagerly, lazily resolve the rest; DIFF against existing upNextItems instead of rebuilding; pull current+next from the shared resolver/snapshotCache so they aren't re-fetched. Win: shuffle/replace lag (relates Lunara-uww.3.9, Lunara-rhp). Best done on top of the shared resolver.
close_reason: Up Next now reuses resolved rows (text + decoded thumbnail) for carried-over tracks instead of rebuilding all 20 on every queue change; first 5 rows resolved/published eagerly then the tail fills, bounding shuffle/replace latency. Deterministic reuse test via UIImage instance identity across an advance. Full suite green.

title: In-memory decoded-image cache in ArtworkPipeline (NSCache) to avoid re-decoding same art
description: ArtworkPipeline has a disk LRU but NO in-memory decoded-image cache, so every consumer re-reads Data(contentsOf:)+re-decodes the same file (screen NowPlayingScreenViewModel.swift:257, bridge NowPlayingBridge.swift:213, bar+upnext thumbnails). Add an NSCache<NSString,UIImage> layer keyed by the same ownerID/ownerKind/imageKind. NOTE: may be largely SUBSUMED if the shared TrackMetadataResolver caches the decoded images — evaluate after that lands; close as superseded if redundant.
close_reason: Added decoded-thumbnail leg (thumbnailArtwork) to shared NowPlayingResolver — symmetric with fullArtwork's artMemo — instead of an NSCache in ArtworkPipeline. Rationale: post-7.1 the resolver is the single source of truth for decoded images; grids/bar render via AsyncImage(url:) and never decode in-app, and the only other in-app decode (AlbumDetailViewModel 64px) is palette-only/discarded, so a pipeline NSCache would have no consumers. The real remaining redundant decode was Up Next rows: same-album distinct tracks each re-decoded the 120px thumb on every fresh window build (the gap 7.2's per-track row reuse left). New thumbArtMemo (CoalescingMemo cap 20 = window size, shouldCache rejects nil to preserve retry) dedupes per album within a window and across rebuilds. 3 new deterministic tests (=== identity, request-count dedup, screen-level same-album dedup). Full suite 127 green. Staff-reviewed twice (design + impl). Local-only branch, not pushed.

title: Non-square album artwork overflows its square cell in grid views
description:
On the Albums grid (and other album/artwork grids), albums whose artwork is not square (e.g. landscape 'Buhloone Mind State', 'Dead Fish In A Can') render at their native aspect ratio and bleed outside the card bounds, overlapping neighboring cells and the title/subtitle text.

Root cause: in the artwork view the image uses .resizable().scaledToFill().frame(maxWidth:.infinity, maxHeight:.infinity) inside a ZStack that then gets .aspectRatio(1,.fit).clipped(). The inner .frame(maxHeight:.infinity) on a scaledToFill image lets the image drive the ZStack's layout, so the square aspectRatio/clipped on the container does not reliably constrain it — non-square art overflows.

Affected (same duplicated pattern):
- Lunara/Views/Library/LibraryGridView.swift (artworkView, ~L162-190)
- Lunara/Views/Collection/CollectionDetailView.swift (albumArtworkView)
- Lunara/Views/TagFilter/TagFilterView.swift (albumArtworkView)
- Lunara/Views/Artist/ArtistDetailView.swift (albumArtworkView)
- also check: ArtistsListView, CollectionsListView, PlaylistDetailView, PlaylistsListView
acceptance_criteria: Landscape/portrait album art renders as a centered, cropped square that stays inside its card on the Albums grid and every other album grid; no bleed into neighboring cells or text. Verified on the De La Soul / Dead Fish In A Can albums from the screenshot.
close_reason: New SquareArtworkView (square frame established first via flexible base + aspectRatio, image overlaid with scaledToFill and NO inner flexible frame, then clipped). Adopted in LibraryGridView, ArtistDetailView, TagFilterView, CollectionDetailView album cards + PlaylistDetailView header (same inner-frame pattern). List rows (artists/collections/playlists/track rows) checked — they use clipShape with row-fixed frames and no aspectRatio sizing, not affected. Device QA: check De La Soul 'Buhloone Mind State' / 'Dead Fish In A Can' in the grid.

title: Replace 'Loading albums…' spinner with delay-gated static skeleton grid on CollectionDetail
description: The collection detail screen (CollectionDetailView.swift) currently shows an awkward centered 'Loading albums…' ProgressView (lines 122-127: a labeled spinner wrapped in two Spacers) while the album grid loads. It floats below the finished header card and looks unpolished/janky. Replace it with a skeleton-grid loading state that mirrors the real grid and crossfades into content for a smoother, more premium feel.
design: DECISION: static redacted placeholder grid, delay-gated. Approach in priority order: (1) DELAY-GATE — the real fix. collectionAlbums (LibraryRepo.swift:148) is offline-first SQLite, near-instant when cached; only cold-cache first view hits network. So do NOT render any loading UI until loading has run ~200ms; on the cached path the real grid just appears (no flash, no spinner). Implement via a @State showPlaceholder toggled by a Task.sleep(~200ms) in the view, cancelled when loadingState leaves .loading. (2) LAYOUT-ANCHOR — when shown, placeholder uses the SAME LazyVGrid columns/spacing as the loaded grid (GridItem(.adaptive(min:140,max:220),spacing:16), grid spacing 20), so header + 'Keep Downloaded' button below don't jump. (3) STATIC redacted cells — count-sized via Collection.albumCount (available immediately, no string parse), min(albumCount, 8) cells. Each cell mirrors albumCard shape: square fill block + two short stub lines, drawn on muted backgroundBase/backgroundElevated fills. NO motion (chosen over shimmer/pulse) — so NO reduce-motion branch and zero battery cost. (4) CROSSFADE skeleton group -> real grid by GROUP opacity with .animation(.easeInOut, value: loadingState); fade whole skeleton vs whole grid, NOT per-cell .transition (heavy/janky in LazyVGrid). (5) ACCESSIBILITY — preserve the VoiceOver behavior the current Progress("Loading albums…") gives for free: container gets .accessibilityElement + .accessibilityLabel("Loading albums"); decorative cells .accessibilityHidden(true). Do NOT add min-display-duration — delay-before-show alone is correct for offline-first; a minimum would re-introduce lingering fake cards. Extract a small reusable LunaraSkeleton placeholder view (first skeleton primitive) but wire ONLY CollectionDetail now (YAGNI on global rollout). Likely reuses existing tokens; no new color token required for static fills.
acceptance_criteria: 1. 'Loading albums…' spinner+text removed. 2. On cached/fast load (<~200ms) NO loading UI renders — real grid appears directly (no flash). 3. When load exceeds ~200ms, a STATIC redacted placeholder grid shows, matching real grid columns/spacing, sized min(Collection.albumCount,8). 4. Smooth group-opacity crossfade skeleton->grid, no per-cell pop, no layout jump for header/Keep-Downloaded. 5. VoiceOver announces 'Loading albums' on the placeholder; decorative cells hidden from a11y. 6. No perpetual animation (static) — no reduce-motion handling needed. 7. Error + empty states unchanged. 8. Reusable LunaraSkeleton extracted; only CollectionDetail wired. 9. Builds + existing tests pass.
notes: Files: Lunara/Views/Collection/CollectionDetailView.swift (albumsSection ~119-152, albumCard ~154 for shape reference). Gate: CollectionDetailViewModel.loadingState (.idle/.loading/.loaded/.error); load path loadAlbums sets .loaded after SQLite read (offline-first, LibraryRepo.swift:148). Count: Collection.albumCount (Collection.swift). Tokens: Color.lunara(.backgroundBase/.backgroundElevated/.textSecondary) in LunaraSemanticColors/LunaraVisualTokens — no shimmer token, none needed for static. Codebase has ZERO reduce-motion handling today (avoided by choosing static). Origin: screenshot feedback from Tim 2026-06-07, 'Albums from 2025'. Visual treatment chosen via review: static redacted (over shimmer/pulse).
close_reason: Spinner removed. Skeleton grid: 200ms delay-gate via @State+task (cached loads show no loading UI), same LazyVGrid geometry, static redacted LunaraSkeleton cells sized min(max(albumCount,1),8), group-opacity crossfade on loadingState, VoiceOver 'Loading albums' + cells hidden. LunaraSkeleton extracted as reusable component; only CollectionDetail wired per design.

title: Stale Now Playing / Up Next UI when starting shuffle from artist page
description: Observed during manual testing (2026-06-07): tapping 'Shuffle' on an artist page presents the Now Playing screen immediately, but the UI shows STALE state from the previously-playing session: the Up Next queue shows the old queue for a brief moment, and the current song / album art / elapsed time show the PREVIOUS track for even longer. Eventually playback buffers and everything updates to the correct shuffled queue. User: 'i do not want to see the wrong UI' — the screen should show the new queue (or a clean loading/placeholder state) from the moment it appears, never the prior track's metadata.
design:
Likely an optimistic-UI ordering issue: Now Playing is presented before the new queue is committed and the first track is resolved/played. Shuffle path: ArtistDetailViewModel.shuffle() (ArtistDetailViewModel.swift:61) -> actions.shuffleArtist(artist) (ArtistsListViewModel.swift:7 protocol). Investigate:
1. WHO presents Now Playing and WHEN relative to queue replacement — is navigation triggered before QueueManager commits the new items + before the first play() resolves? (QueueManager URL resolution is async; isResolvingPlayback gate exists ~QueueManager.swift:232.)
2. UP NEXT shows old queue briefly -> the queue items array is likely replaced AFTER the screen appears, or the view observes a snapshot updated post-resolve. Confirm the new items are set synchronously before presentation.
3. CURRENT TRACK/ART/TIME persist longer -> NowPlayingScreenViewModel snapshotCache / current-track binding holds the prior track until the engine reports the new currentTrackID (only after async resolve + engine.play). Need to clear/placeholder current-track UI on queue replacement, not wait for engine.
RELATED: this is the same view-vs-engine staleness family as Lunara-2jb (UI not updating on auto-advance). Check whether one root binding fix covers both.
EVIDENCE: ArtistDetailViewModel.swift:55-65; QueueManager.swift:225-241 (play/resolve), :274-317 (prepareNext).
acceptance_criteria: On shuffle (and play-all) from artist page, the Now Playing screen never displays the prior session's track/art/time/queue. It shows correct new-queue content or an explicit loading placeholder until the first track resolves.
close_reason: Queue/track/art staleness fixed by earlier landed work (rhp dedup removal, uww.7.1/7.2 shared resolver + windowed Up Next, wtj two-phase publish; playNow commits items+index synchronously). Remaining sliver fixed here: screen VM elapsed/duration no longer pass through the engine while it is still on the outgoing track — scrubber holds at 0/new-track duration until engine.currentTrackID matches the queue item. Test: elapsedAndDuration_holdAtZeroUntilEngineConfirmsNewTrack. Device QA welcome on the original shuffle-from-artist repro.

title: Bound/evict artworkByAlbumID dictionary
description: LibraryGridViewModel.swift:39 grows unbounded with library size.
design: Bound the unbounded var artworkByAlbumID:[String:URL] (line ~39) with LRU while keeping it an @Observable stored property (SwiftUI still re-renders) and preserving thumbnailURL(for:) read API (line ~116, view line ~161). Add private var artworkLRU:[String] (recency, most-recent last) + static artworkCacheCapacity=300. New private func storeArtwork(_:for:) used in loadThumbnailIfNeeded success (line ~141): move id to end of artworkLRU, set dict, while count>capacity removeFirst() from both. In thumbnailURL(for:) on hit move id to end (mark used). Eviction must not touch pendingArtworkAlbumIDs. Consider making capacity an init param defaulted to 300 so tests can pass a small value (avoid 300 awaited resolutions). FILES: LibraryGridViewModel.swift (optional new +ArtworkCache.swift), tests LibraryGridViewModelTests.swift. OUT_OF_SCOPE: dont touch ArtworkPipeline/on-disk cache, loadThumbnailIfNeeded fetch flow, pending dedupe semantics, AsyncImage usage, or other VMs artwork dicts.

LRU: recently-requested IDs retained, oldest dropped (test). pendingArtworkAlbumIDs doesnt leak across eviction (returns to empty). Re-requesting an evicted album re-resolves and re-inserts; existing artwork tests pass.
notes: TESTS first (LibraryGridViewModelTests.swift) using waitForArtworkResolution helper: (1) resolve cap+5 distinct albums -> artworkByAlbumID.count<=capacity (inject small capacity for speed); (2) LRU: resolve cap+1, first id evicted (thumbnailURL nil), newest present; touch secondOldest then resolve one more -> touched survives, next-oldest evicted; (3) pending cleanup: after eviction storm no stuck pending (re-request issues fresh thumbnailRequests). DEPENDENCY: after 4.1 (paging makes dict track scrolled window; 4.2-first would be masked by load-all flooding).

title: Fix orphaned-file race + album download atomicity

Startup orphan sweep removeOrphanedFiles() (no-op while downloads active) wired in AppCoordinator. Bonus: cancel landing during the last track's save no longer marks the album complete. title: Fix album palette double-decode

If 1.3 already moved this off-main, keep inside same Task.detached and just swap sizing to 64. Set artworkURL=url before decode. FILES: edit AlbumDetailViewModel.swift (loadArtwork) only. OUT_OF_SCOPE: dont change ArtworkPaletteExtractor 50x50 sampling, the view display path, artworkURL semantics, or other VMs.

title: Verify MBID cache actually speeds radar sweeps — observed no speedup on device
description: Device QA 2026-06-11 step 5: second radar sweep felt the same speed (~2-3s/artist) as the first, but with artist_mbids cached (Lunara-be2, PR #127) per-artist cost should drop from 2 throttled MusicBrainz requests (search + release-groups) to 1 (~halved). INVESTIGATE: (1) add a per-artist log/telemetry line in RadarService.upcomingAlbums(for:) showing cache HIT/MISS and elapsed ms (PlaybackTelemetry-style span or os Logger) so the next device run produces evidence; (2) verify rows actually land in artist_mbids on device (saveArtistMBID write path — try? swallows errors by design, a silent failure would force the search every sweep; check migration v13 ran); (3) confirm the second sweep wasn't gated/queued behind the first (refresh() guards isRefreshing — a pull during a running sweep is silently dropped, so Tim may have timed the SAME sweep twice); (4) rule out latency dominance: throttle is 1s BETWEEN requests, so search+fetch is at least ~2s, fetch-only at least ~1s + RTT — if MusicBrainz RTT is ~1s, observed difference shrinks but should still be visible. title: Investigate: edit album metadata from the app (tags/moods/feelings, rating, release date) written back to Plex

title: BUG: TrackCache failure 'falls back' to a remote URL AVAudioPlayer cannot play
description: QueueManager.playCurrentItem (QueueManager.swift:218-224): when TrackCache.prepare throws, playURL stays the remote https URL and is handed to engine.play — but AVAudioPlayer(contentsOf:) cannot stream remote URLs, so the 'direct play' fallback comment is wrong; the load fails and the stream-recovery path re-resolves (which will re-attempt the same cache). Net effect: a cache failure means a silent retry loop instead of a graceful fallback. Decide: either treat cache failure as the play failure directly (clearer error, no dead fallback), or retry prepare once before failing. Low priority: cache failures are rare (disk full).
close_reason: trackCache.prepare failure now propagates as the play failure (lastError set, item retained for retry) instead of handing AVAudioPlayer a remote URL it cannot stream and burning the one-shot recovery on a doomed load. Test drives a real failed loopback download.

title: Defense-in-depth: engine validates next-track buffer is loadable before crossfading
description: Follow-up from Lunara-uww.3.6 staff review. CrossfadeEngine.beginCrossfade (CrossfadeEngine.swift:330) and the immediate-swap branch of handleTrackEnded (~:414) fade into the inactive slot without re-checking the underlying source is still healthy. 3.6 fixes the download-driven case via clearPreparedNext, but ANY dead next buffer (e.g. resolve/play races, file evicted by OS) could still fade into silence. Add a health check (re-stat file URL / verify prepareToPlay) at fade time; on failure, fall through to the idle/advance path instead of fading into silence. Orthogonal to DownloadManager signaling — protects all sources.
design: AVAudioPlayer won't error on play() of an unlinked-but-open file, so needs a real existence/health check, not just relying on play() failure.
close_reason: PlayerSlotProtocol.isReadyForPlayback (player loaded + file re-stat for file URLs, since AVAudioPlayer plays unlinked files as silence). beginCrossfade discards a dead staged buffer via clearPreparedNext; handleTrackEnded immediate-swap falls through to the idle path so the queue re-resolves fresh. 2 engine tests.

title: Investigate sustained-playback footprint drift + outgoing slot release
description: REPURPOSED 2026-06-07 from 'cap concurrent loads' (original RAM-spike premise disproved — see Lunara-uww.2.1). On-device telemetry surfaced two real-but-low-severity signals on a SINGLE track at constant slots==2: (1) footMB climbs +27.7MB (~3.2MB/min) monotonically over ~9min, unrelated to the 2nd slot (quartile medians 149.7->157.6->167.3->169.6), never returning to the 145-150 baseline; (2) crossfadeBegin fired with NO matching crossfadeComplete and slots never dropped back to 1 — outgoing slot not released in-log. Investigate slot-release path (completeCrossfade -> stop -> nil) and the drift source (buffer growth?).
design: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed in code 2026-06-07): crossfade completion is driven by the OUTGOING player's clock. beginCrossfade() sets crossfadeStartTime=activeSlot.elapsed (CrossfadeEngine.swift:332); updateCrossfade() computes progress=(activeSlot.elapsed - crossfadeStartTime)/crossfadeDuration (line 345-346) and only calls completeCrossfade() when progress>=1.0 (line 351). activeSlot.elapsed == AVAudioPlayer.currentTime (PlayerSlot.swift:15), which RESETS toward 0 when the file finishes. If the fade doesn't finish before the outgoing file ends (small runway: telemetry shows crossfadeBegin at 235s on a 247s track = 12s), currentTime resets, progress goes negative, never reaches 1.0 -> completeCrossfade() never runs -> isCrossfading stuck true -> BOTH slots pinned forever (the 2.2 leak) -> outgoing slot never stopped/nil'd. Compounding: handleTrackEnded() is suppressed by its !isCrossfading guard (line 385) so nothing recovers, and the incoming slot is left at volume~0 (silent) + trackID never advances (Now Playing freezes). Matches telemetry exactly: slots stuck=2, trackID stuck=85081, no crossfadeComplete, state=playing for 5min past track end. Drift finding (~3MB/min) is SEPARATE and likely benign warmup: quartile deltas decelerate (+7.9,+9.7,+2.3) and footprint dipped to 159 at end -> plateauing ~170MB, not a runaway leak.
notes: Headroom was vast this session (min availMB=3202, ~3.2GB free; footprint peaked 181MB) — NO jetsam risk, hence low priority. Data caveat: log is a single 9-min single-track session, only ONE slots==1 sample, zero appBackground/appForeground/skip/stop events. Need a multi-track session with completed crossfades + a backgrounded stretch to characterize cause. Also: engine never advanced trackID, so this log gives no corroboration for Lunara-2jb (UI auto-advance bug).
close_reason: Fixed the outgoing-slot-release wedge. Crossfade completion now driven by the incoming slot's monotonic clock (immune to the outgoing AVAudioPlayer.currentTime reset at EOF), completeCrossfade made idempotent, handleTrackEnded force-completes a mid-fade crossfade, and cancelActiveCrossfade now keeps the preloaded next track loaded so a seek mid-fade re-triggers correctly. 5 regression tests in CrossfadeEngineTests; full suite 405/405 green; verified on device (end-of-track advance + seek-backward-mid-fade both correct). Sustained-playback drift (~3MB/min) deferred as benign: it decelerates/plateaus (~170MB) with 3.2GB headroom — revisit only if a longer multi-track log shows real unbounded growth.
